body.statement: For every \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\) with \(d_n=d\) fixed, the balanced-mass and nondegenerate-variance conditions remain in force, and \(thm:local-linearization\) and \(thm:endpoint-equivalence\) reduce to the classical efficient-influence-function central limit theorem, ratio-consistent variance estimation, and Wald interval for the ATE with fixed discrete covariates.
body.justification: The fixed-alphabet reduction is the required sanity check against regular semiparametric ATE inference.
body.gap: Hahn1998 and ChernozhukovEtAl2018DML give the known fixed-complexity efficiency benchmark; the proposition verifies that the new interval does not alter that limit.
body.consumer: Readers can interpret the robust procedure as a strict regime extension of familiar ATE inference rather than a different estimand.
